rows.name: spoken-why-warps-frozen-5
rows.question: Why
rows.answer: Because threads in a warp share GPU execution resources, similar control flow and consecutive memory accesses make those resources more efficient. When threads take different branches, the GPU executes each path with nonparticipating threads inactive, reducing useful parallel work. Accessing consecutive memory locations lets the GPU combine requests into fewer memory transactions, improving throughput.

Advancing the read and write indices modulo 17 preserves FIFO order through wraparound.
